evals.prompt: Our biggest customer (a 40-person agency) just emailed asking us to 'add a full reporting dashboard with custom charts' to our project management SaaS. Sales wants to say yes today. I'm the PM and we're 2 designers and 5 devs. How should I handle this?
evals.expected_output: A shaping-first response: a soft 'interesting, maybe some day' instead of a commitment; digging into when and why the customer needed reports (the moment the workflow breaks); an explicit appetite decision (small or big batch) set before any solution; a warning that 'full dashboard' is a grab-bag; and no backlog entry.
assertions: Advises against committing or saying yes before the work is shaped
Recommends finding the specific moment or use case behind the request (asks 'when' or 'what's really going wrong'), not collecting feature specs
Sets or asks for an appetite (a time budget such as 2 or 6 weeks) before proposing a solution, and distinguishes it from an estimate
Does not suggest adding the request to a backlog
Flags 'full reporting dashboard' as too broad and suggests narrowing it to one problem

evals.prompt: Can you review this pitch before Thursday's betting table? It's at evals/files/bad-pitch.md
evals.expected_output: A pitch review that names the concrete defects: a solution-first, story-less problem; an appetite given as an estimate and longer than one cycle; wireframe-level detail; open questions pushed to the designer; an unpatched rabbit hole; 'None' for no-gos; the '2.0' grab-bag. It recommends sending the pitch back to shaping rather than betting on it.
assertions: States the pitch is not ready for the betting table / should go back to shaping
Identifies that the appetite is an estimate (hours/months) and exceeds a six-week cycle
Identifies the problem section lacks a specific story and leads with a solution
Flags pixel/hex/wireframe detail in the solution as over-specified
Flags 'TBD / the designer will figure it out' as an unresolved hole
Flags the performance rabbit hole as listed without a patch or decision
Flags the empty/None no-gos and the '2.0' grab-bag

evals.prompt: We're in week 5 of a 6-week cycle on 'Team Calendars'. Scopes: Event CRUD (done), Month Grid (downhill, ~80%), Recurring Events (still uphill, we haven't figured out editing a single occurrence), Timezone Handling (uphill), Invites Email (downhill). My CTO wants to just extend the project 3 more weeks. Is that the right call?
evals.expected_output: A clear recommendation against a default extension: uphill scopes at the deadline mean a hole in the shaping, so the circuit breaker applies. Scope-hammer Recurring Events and Timezones (cut, or ship without them if they're not must-haves), ship what's downhill, compared against the baseline, and put the uphill parts back on the shaping track for a future bet. An extension is only justified when all remaining work is must-have and downhill.
assertions: Recommends against the 3-week extension
Explains that uphill work (unsolved problems) at the deadline is the key reason not to extend
States the extension criteria: remaining work must be true must-haves AND all downhill
Proposes scope hammering / cutting Recurring Events and/or Timezone Handling and shipping the rest
Suggests re-shaping the unsolved parts as a new pitch for a future betting table rather than continuing

evals.prompt: We just bet on the Autopay pitch (evals/files/good-pitch.md) for next cycle. Please break it into Jira tickets with estimates and assign them to Priya (design), Marco and Jun (backend) so they can start Monday.
evals.expected_output: A respectful push-back on pre-splitting and assigning tasks (the paper-shredder problem), explaining that the team takes the whole project and discovers its tasks. Instead: a kick-off plan, orientation expectations, a suggested first piece to integrate end to end (core, small, novel, e.g. the Autopay checkbox wired through to a saved state), and guidance that scopes will emerge around the end of week 1. If Jira is mandatory, create tickets per scope as they're discovered, owned by the team.
assertions: Does not produce a full up-front task breakdown with per-person assignments and estimates as the main deliverable
Explains that the team should own the whole project and discover tasks (assign projects, not tasks)
Recommends a first vertical slice integrated end to end early (roughly the first week) and names a candidate from the pitch
Mentions scopes emerging from the work (not planned up front) and/or offers a per-scope ticket compromise
Includes or offers a kick-off message/plan

evals.prompt: We're a 3-person startup (me as founder/designer, two engineers). I read about Shape Up — should we do six-week cycles with a betting table and cool-downs?
evals.expected_output: Adoption advice scaled to size: a team that small can drop most of the structure (fixed cycles, cool-down, formal pitches, betting table) but should keep the phases deliberate: set an appetite, shape, bet, build, and know which hat you're wearing. Bets can vary in length. It suggests a concrete way to start and notes when to add structure as the team grows.
assertions: Says a 2-3 person team doesn't need the full formal structure (cycles/cool-down/betting table/formal pitches)
Insists they still shape work and set appetites before building
Mentions being deliberate about which role or phase ('hat') you are in
Gives a concrete first step or lightweight process to try
